name: T&G Global Limited
overview: T&G Global is a 125-year-old New Zealand-headquartered grower, marketer and global distributor of premium fresh produce, best known for its ENVY, JAZZ and JOLI branded apples. Following a mid-2026 strategic review the group is narrowing its focus to two core divisions - Apples (integrated genetics-to-consumer branded apple platform) and VentureFruit (plant-variety IP licensing across apples, pears, berries and dragon fruit) - after agreeing to sell its domestic New Zealand fresh produce, Fijian and Pacific Islands export businesses. T&G is majority owned (~74%) by BayWa AG of Germany via BayWa Global Produce GmbH, which is itself in financial distress and has been trying to sell its T&G stake since mid-2025.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned mainly from selling own-grown and licensed-grower fresh produce (apples, and historically tomatoes/berries/citrus/stone fruit), supplemented by commissions/services on third-party produce and, increasingly, IP royalties and plant-variety licence fees from VentureFruit. The strategic pivot underway is explicitly from low-margin, volume-driven produce trading toward higher-margin branded apples and IP/royalty income, since a fixed royalty or licence fee is earned regardless of who grows the fruit, insulating T&G from some direct horticultural/trading risk.

revenue_streams.name: Sale of produce (Apples, own & licensed growing)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - supermarkets, wholesalers, importers/distributors and foodservice globally; licensed growers as counterparties for VentureFruit IP
business_model.geographic_mix: H1 FY2026 revenue ~2.6% up YoY to NZ$572.3m; FY2025 revenue by region: Asia $510.2m, UK/Europe/Africa $496.6m, Aotearoa New Zealand $348.9m, Australia & Pacific Islands $116.5m, Americas $86.4m (total group revenue, pre-discontinued-ops restatement, $1.6bn for FY2025)

segments.name: Apples
segments.description: Growing, packing, cool-storing, marketing and global sale of ENVY, JAZZ and JOLI branded apples via own orchards and an extensive independent licensed-grower network in 13+ countries.

segments.name: T&G Fresh
segments.description: Historically New Zealand/Fijian/Pacific domestic fresh produce (tomatoes, berries, citrus, stone fruit) trading and distribution; the NZ, Fijian and Pacific Islands export operations were classified as held-for-sale/discontinued from 30 June 2026 and sold via three separate transactions (NZ business to the Turner family/J&P Turner, Fiji/Pacific to Bidfood, 51% of Unearthed Produce Limited to its minority holders). The retained rump is the Australian growing/trading business including the Queensland blueberry farm, to be folded into VentureFruit.

segments.name: VentureFruit
segments.description: Global plant-variety rights management and commercialisation business, licensing apple, pear, berry and dragon fruit genetics to growers worldwide and enforcing IP/PVR protection (including recent Chinese court and Seed Law wins on the ENVY variety Scilate).

segments.name: Other/International Trading
segments.description: Residual trading elements of the former International Trading segment not yet reallocated to other segments.

main_competitors: Oppenheimer Group (North American produce distribution, T&G minority-owned partner)
Rivals in licensed premium apple varieties (e.g. Pink Lady/Apple and Pear Australia, Cripps varieties)
Regional apple growers/marketers in Washington State, Chile, South Africa, Europe
Generic/commodity apple growers competing on price
competitive_position.market_position: Global leader in premium branded apples via ENVY (first NZ apple brand to reach NZ$1bn cumulative retail sales) and JAZZ (No.1 imported apple brand in Japan); a niche but growing player in plant-variety IP licensing through VentureFruit; historically also a mid-sized domestic New Zealand fresh produce wholesaler/distributor, now being exited.

moat_factors.description: Exclusive/licensed rights to ENVY (Scilate), JAZZ (Scifresh) and JOLI (PREMA019) varieties, reinforced by successful IP enforcement (e.g. Chinese Supreme People's Court ruling protecting Scilate) and NZ Government's proposed PVR Act amendments extending protection terms by five years.

ENVY US household penetration rose from 12% to 15% YoY (~19.9m households); JAZZ dominant in UK and Japan; but consumer apple purchasing remains price-sensitive and substitutable versus other premium varieties.

End-to-end platform from genetics/growing through post-harvest to in-market demand generation across 55+ countries provides supply-chain control and flexibility to route fruit to the best market, but also fixed-asset intensity.
Extensive licensed-grower network across NZ and internationally provides supply scale beyond T&G's own orchards, but growers can be courted by competing brand owners once licences expire.

Multi-year orchard planting cycles and royalty/licence agreements lock in growers for the life of an orchard block (15-20+ years), creating durable but not permanent recurring licence/royalty revenue for VentureFruit.

weaknesses: Thin, volatile margins on non-branded produce trading (T&G Fresh/International Trading segments were loss-making or barely profitable for years before divestment)
Heavy reliance on weather-dependent, single-region NZ apple crop (Hawke's Bay, Nelson) for a large share of Apples volume
VentureFruit remains loss-making at the operating level (-$6.8m H1 FY2026) despite revenue growth, and is highly sensitive to growers' capex/planting appetite
Small free float and NZX micro-cap illiquidity, with ~74% held by a single distressed foreign parent
Limited pricing power on generic/non-branded fruit versus retailers and large global distributors

growth_drivers: Global premium apple category forecast to grow from US$23.5bn (2024) to US$52.7bn by 2035 (CAGR ~7.6-8.4%), with T&G's premium portfolio targeted to outgrow the category
ENVY brand momentum: surpassed NZ$1bn cumulative retail sales; US household penetration up from 12% to 15% YoY; strong volume growth in Vietnam (+34%), China (+26%) and Thailand (+10%) in H1 FY2026
Launch of JOLI apples (first market Vietnam, later 2026) targeting the 'family sharing' consumer need with very favourable consumer testing

VentureFruit's shift from produce trading to a royalty/licence model - new global head licences, US berries strategy (160,000 new berry plant orders, well ahead of target) via California Giant Berry Farms partnership, and expansion into UK/Poland berry genetics
New Zealand-India Free Trade Agreement removing/reducing the prior 50% tariff, opening India's >US$1bn premium apple market to both Apples and VentureFruit
Post-divestment balance sheet simplification: proceeds from the T&G Fresh sale earmarked to repay debt, including a NZ$20.8m BayWa loan, freeing capital and management focus for Apples/VentureFruit
Continued yield/quality gains from maturing ENVY plantings (NZ crop volume +24% in 2026) and post-harvest efficiency investment (Whakatu, Hawke's Bay, Nelson facilities)

business.description: Cyclone Gabrielle (Feb 2023) destroyed ~13% of Hawke's Bay planted hectares, drove a NZ$45.6m operating loss that year and delayed strategy delivery by 18+ months; El Nino conditions flagged as a risk to the 2026/27 crop.
Significant reliance on Hawke's Bay and Nelson growing regions and on a defined set of licensed growers; any regional crop failure, disease or labour shortage materially affects volumes.

Simultaneously completing three T&G Fresh divestments, integrating the retained Australian berry business into VentureFruit, and scaling a still loss-making VentureFruit creates meaningful transition/execution risk.

business.risk: Thin margins in non-core produce trading
business.description: T&G Fresh and Other/International Trading have a history of low or negative operating margins, underscoring why the business is being exited but also showing the fragility of the produce-trading model the company built its scale on.
Global supermarket chains have significant buying power over branded and unbranded fruit alike, compressing achievable margins.

financial.description: Group borrowings ~NZ$308m and lease liabilities ~NZ$166m at 30 June 2026 (total financial liabilities ~NZ$731m) against total equity of NZ$467m; bank facilities were only secured through to 2028 partly because of BayWa's own instability.

Revenue is earned in USD, EUR, GBP and various Asian currencies while T&G reports in NZD, creating translation and transaction FX risk not fully offset by hedging (large cash-flow-hedge swings evident in H1 FY2026 other comprehensive income).

Property, plant and equipment (~NZ$392-424m) includes orchard land and buildings carried at revalued amounts; declines in rural land values or orchard productivity assumptions could trigger impairments (already saw a NZ$34.4m impairment on the T&G Fresh disposal group in H1 FY2026).
A NZ$20.8m loan from BayWa is being repaid from divestment proceeds, but the relationship with a financially stressed parent creates counterparty and governance complexity.

regulatory.description: The sale of the NZ fresh produce business to J&P Turner (the Turner family) requires NZ Commerce Commission clearance (decision targeted 26 August 2026); a block or delay would disrupt the announced simplification and debt-reduction plan.
Pending NZ PVR Act amendments are expected to strengthen VentureFruit's IP protections, but the outcome and timing of the legislative process is not guaranteed.

High tariffs (e.g. historically 50% into India) and phytosanitary/market-access barriers in Asia and the Middle East can disrupt export flows, as seen with Middle East conflict disruption to apple exports in H1 FY2026.

macro.description: Premium apples carry a price premium over commodity fruit; cost-of-living pressures were cited as dampening demand in some markets (T&G Fresh, UK/Europe oversupply).
Global shipping/freight rate volatility and Middle East conflict-driven oil price increases directly affect landed cost of exported fruit.
Sizeable floating-rate borrowings and seasonal funding facilities (used to fund grower advances and working capital) make the business sensitive to interest rate movements.

macro.risk: BayWa AG parent distress / forced-sale overhang
macro.description: Majority shareholder BayWa AG is undergoing a major debt restructuring in Germany (~EUR2.7bn hole, seeking ~EUR1bn in creditor debt waivers) and needs to realise ~EUR300m from selling its ~74% T&G stake; the sale process (Goldman Sachs-run since March 2026) has stalled because minority shareholder Joy Wing Mau Group (~20% stake) is withholding consent, creating an extended period of ownership uncertainty, potential forced/distressed-sale dynamics, and possible governance or strategic disruption for T&G shareholders.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global premium apple category is a structurally growing niche within a broadly mature global apple market, forecast to grow at roughly 7.6-8.4% CAGR through the mid-2030s on rising urbanisation, health/wellness trends and consumers' willingness to pay for consistent quality/taste; broader fresh produce trading (T&G's legacy business) is a low-growth, low-margin, highly competitive commodity industry.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High agricultural/weather cyclicality (crop yield and quality vary year to year) layered on moderate consumer-discretionary cyclicality for premium-priced fruit; results are also seasonal, with Apples generating most revenue mid-year around the Southern Hemisphere harvest.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate to high - seasonal funding lines, grower advances and long-term borrowings are largely floating rate, and orchard development is capital intensive.
key_input_costs: Ocean freight/shipping and oil-price-linked logistics costs
Insurance (crop and property, elevated post-Cyclone Gabrielle)

recent_developments.event: Group entered sale and purchase agreements (31 July 2026) for the NZ fresh produce, Fijian and Pacific Islands export businesses, split across three buyers (Turner family/J&P Turner for NZ fresh produce; Bidfood Pacific Islands for Fiji/Pacific exports; Pukekawa Holdings/Ashsadeep for the 51% stake in Unearthed Produce Limited), subject to NZ Commerce Commission clearance (decision targeted 26 August 2026).

H1 FY2026 interim result: revenue up 2.6% to NZ$572.3m, operating profit up 30.3% to NZ$11.6m, but a reported net loss of NZ$30.5m (vs NZ$1.7m profit pcp) driven by a NZ$34.4m impairment on reclassifying the divested T&G Fresh businesses as held-for-sale/discontinued.
ENVY apple brand surpassed NZ$1 billion in cumulative global retail sales, the first apple brand from New Zealand to do so; ENVY US household penetration rose from 12% to 15% year-on-year.

BayWa AG's sale of its ~74% T&G stake (run by Goldman Sachs since March 2026, targeting ~EUR300m proceeds as part of BayWa's broader EUR1bn-plus debt-restructuring) stalled after minority shareholder Joy Wing Mau Group (~20% stake) withheld consent required to clear the transaction.

BayWa AG first announced its intention to sell its majority T&G shareholding as part of its own financial restructuring in Germany; T&G appointed Goldman Sachs as financial adviser to assess strategic options.

FY2025 annual result: revenue grew to NZ$1.6bn (from NZ$1.4bn) and operating profit rose to NZ$46.9m (from NZ$12.7m), Apples now 67% of group revenue; management secured refinancing through to 2028 given the BayWa ownership uncertainty.
China's Supreme People's Court upheld a landmark ruling protecting T&G's Scilate (ENVY) plant variety rights, reinforcing VentureFruit's IP enforcement position in a key growth market.
Restructured North American shareholding arrangements, increasing the stake in Asia-export-focused Delica North America while reducing the holding in diversified produce distributor Oppenheimer.

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report (August 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report (February 2026)

items.target: Reduction expected in year-end results due to divestment of most of T&G Fresh
items.notes: Management explicitly flagged that the divestment of most of T&G Fresh will reduce reported group revenue for the balance of FY2026, offset by debt reduction from sale proceeds; no specific numeric revenue guidance given.

items.target: Repay debt including a NZ$20.8m BayWa loan using T&G Fresh sale proceeds
items.notes: Framed as strengthening the balance sheet to free capital/management focus for Apples and VentureFruit.

items.target: Continue growing market share in the global premium apples category (long-term ~8% CAGR category growth) and accelerate VentureFruit's licensing pipeline, particularly in Asia and India
items.notes: No specific numeric targets provided; qualitative outlook only, with an El Nino risk flagged for the 2026/27 NZ apple crop.
Secured in FY2025 partly in response to ownership uncertainty created by BayWa's announced intention to sell its stake.

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Benedikt Mangold and CEO Gareth Edgecombe stated the T&G Fresh divestments will 'simplify our corporate structure and business overall to focus on the significant growth opportunities we see in apples and intellectual property,' while confirming BayWa's intention to exit its shareholding remains, with Goldman Sachs appointed to assess strategic options for T&G separately from the T&G Fresh sale process.

bull_case: Clear strategic pivot from low-margin produce trading toward a higher-margin, IP-and-brand-led Apples/VentureFruit model, evidenced by ENVY crossing NZ$1bn in cumulative retail sales and improving segment margins

VentureFruit represents an emerging royalty/licensing revenue stream (new global head licences, US berries momentum, Chinese IP court win) that could re-rate the business toward a higher-multiple, capital-light model over time

Divestment of the historically low-margin T&G Fresh domestic business simplifies the group, reduces debt, and lets management concentrate capital on the fastest-growing, highest-return segment (Apples)
Structural tailwind from the global premium apple category, forecast to grow at a 7.6-8.4% CAGR through the mid-2030s, with T&G's branded portfolio (ENVY, JAZZ, JOLI) well positioned to outgrow it

A resolution of the BayWa ownership overhang (whether via a clean sale, buyer emerging, or Joy Wing Mau consolidating/negotiating) could act as a catalyst and remove a persistent valuation discount tied to ownership uncertainty
bear_case: BayWa's distressed parent situation is an unresolved overhang - the Goldman Sachs-run sale process has stalled on minority shareholder Joy Wing Mau's refusal to consent, leaving T&G's ultimate ownership, free float and strategic direction uncertain for an extended period

Very low free float and NZX micro-cap illiquidity (BayWa ~74%, Joy Wing Mau ~20%) mean minority shareholders have limited influence and the stock is thinly traded, exposing it to headline risk from BayWa/German press coverage unrelated to T&G's own operating performance

Horticulture is inherently exposed to weather shocks (Cyclone Gabrielle wiped out ~13% of planted Hawke's Bay hectares in 2023 and set the strategy back 18+ months); El Nino risk is already flagged for the 2026/27 crop
VentureFruit remains operating-loss-making despite the growth narrative, and its revenue is directly linked to (and therefore not diversifying away from) the cyclicality of the core Apples business

Execution risk around simultaneously closing three divestment transactions (subject to Commerce Commission clearance), reorganising the retained Australian berry assets into VentureFruit, and sustaining the still-nascent IP-licensing growth story
